question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two independent continuous random variables whose marginal density functions are as follows:

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{9}x, & \,0\le x\le 3, \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\,\,{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡y, & \,0\le y\le \frac{\pi }{2}, \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Find $P(X\le 2,Y\le 3).$

current_example.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two independent continuous random variables whose marginal density functions are as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14274305/assets/5ff2340d6c6116981965d581b5b60a8046a20979e141d3f6ed3e456079eed987.svg)

Find $P(X \geq 3, Y \leq  2).$
current_example.worked_solution:
Two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ with joint probability density function $f(x,y)$ are independent if and only if 

$$
f(x, y) = f_X(x) \cdot f_Y (y)
$$

 

for all possible values $x$ and $y,$ where $f_X(x)$ and $f_Y (y)$ are the marginal probability density functions for $X$ and $Y,$ respectively.

Since our random variables are independent, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & ={f}_{X}(x)\cdot {f}_{Y}(y) \\  & =\frac{10}{3{x}^{2}}\cdot \frac{1}{4}y \\  & =\frac{5y}{6{x}^{2}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $(x,y) \in \left[2,5\right]\times \left[1,3\right].$ Therefore, the full expression for $f(x,y)$ is

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14274305/assets/5f7943e8b9a1bb0f612edf13cc1320e6467781bda7a793f5edefdea660ce4dc4.svg)

Finally, the required probability is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\ge 3,Y\le 2) & ={\int }_{3}^{5}[{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{5y}{6{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{5}\frac{5}{6{x}^{2}}{[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{1}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{5}\frac{5}{6{x}^{2}}(\frac{3}{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{5}\frac{5}{4{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[-\frac{5}{4x}]}_{3}^{5} \\  & =-\frac{5}{4}(\frac{1}{5}-\frac{1}{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$
